notes: v2.83 (2026-11-08, afternoon run): 82nd tower 'Coat' (hood over shoulders and body with sleeve edges over a hem row, 30 blocks, 4 clusters sizes 10/8/6/6, all 4 colours, no singletons) + 79th co-play prompt (Montessori coat flip on the floor, zipper up, hood by his feet, arms in, flip over his head; grown-up starts the zip, he pulls it up; hang it on its hook; coat goes on first — coat, boots, hat, then mittens). Coat-play research: at 2, a child can take off an unfastened coat, find armholes, and put on a front-opening coat (no fastening); the coat flip is the canonical self-dressing move; undressing is easier than dressing, so taking it off and hanging it up is the part he can do himself. v2.82 (2026-11-08, morning run): 81st tower 'Boots' (two pull-handles over two shafts on a wide feet band over a two-colour sole row, 22 blocks, 4 clusters sizes 8/8/3/3, all 4 colours, no singletons) + 78th co-play prompt (pull rain boots on by their handles, stomp in a puddle, take them off and line them up by the door; boots go on second — coat, boots, hat, then mittens). Boots-play research: oversized pull handles plus a wide opening make pulling boots on a solo job for a toddler; stomping in puddles is the payoff; light and flexible beats heavy and stiff. v2.81 (2026-11-07, late run): 80th tower 'Hat' (pom + dome + brim band + two hanging earflaps, 22 blocks, 5 clusters sizes 6/6/6/2/2, all 4 colours, no singletons) + 77th co-play prompt (put a warm hat on/off, check it covers the ears, shake-head/look-up fit test, put it on a teddy too; dressing order coat, boots, hat, then mittens). Hat-play research: at 2, putting on a hat is one of the first dressing skills a child can actually do; the hat that stays on covers the ears and sits above the eyebrows; dressing is taught in small steps through dress-up play with no time pressure. v2.80 (2026-11-07, afternoon run): 79th tower 'Scarf' (rounded top over wide bands on two fringed ends, 22 blocks, 5 clusters sizes 6/6/6/2/2, all 4 colours, no singletons) + 76th co-play prompt (drape a scarf like a cape, wrap a teddy snug, hide-and-find peek-a-boo; never tight around a little neck). Scarf-play research: cover/uncover builds object permanence, pulling off builds fine-motor grip, and a scarf is an open-ended prop (cape, doll blanket, den roof). Block Pop replaced the 9-activity menu game on 2026-10-13 (kept as classic.html). One deep mechanic: tap a color cannon, blast matching block clusters, clear the tower. v2.79 (2026-11-07, parent report + browser test): fixed the leftover colored dot after a pop. The block and its white glyph were being removed correctly — the dot was a stuck pop particle. burst() used `var p` in a loop, so all six onfinish handlers closed over the same variable and only the last particle was ever removed; the other five sat at full opacity in the middle of the popped block (browser test: 4 blue dots, one per popped block, still there at 6s). Fixed with the same per-particle IIFE capture the ball code already uses, plus fill:'forwards' and a 900ms sweep so no particle can outlive the pop. Verified with a node closure test (old code removes 1 of 6, new code removes 6 of 6). v2.78 grew the cutscene rotation to 3 movies and retired frog-garden. Content-only repo: no personal data beyond the first name.
